sentences.text: Long ago, to buy one chicken, you had to haul a sack of rice to market.
People swapped goods: rice for fish, salt for cloth, goats for wheat.
He walks all the way to the docks to find a fisherman.
But the fisherman shakes his head.
Then the farmer finds a shoemaker, who wants a goat.
Half a day gone, sore feet, a full sack of rice, and still no fish.
You see, barter only works when two people want each other's things at once.
Instead, people used shells, salt and metal.
Around two thousand six hundred years ago, Lydia, now Turkey, struck some of the earliest coins.
A thousand years ago, China printed paper money.
Now we just tap a phone.
So from rice to a single tap, money keeps changing with us.
If money vanished tomorrow, what would you trade for lunch?
